oc-talk

Two-way cross-session messaging for OpenCode: send an addressed synthetic note to a live session and read the reply.

## Install Add the plugin to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` and restart OpenCode: ```json { "plugins": ["oc-talk"] } ``` The plugin reads the harness service state and needs no other config. A default install registers exactly two tools: `talk_send` and `talk_inbox`. ## Use it Send a message, then read the session: ```text talk_send { "session": "build lane", "text": "Run the tests and report failures." } → { "id": "msg_0f3c…", "sessionID": "ses_9a1…", "from": { "sessionID": "ses_caller", "title": "dispatcher" }, "replyTo": "ses_caller", "delivered": true } talk_inbox { "session": "ses_caller" } → { "sessionID": "ses_caller", "messages": [ … ] } ``` The message enters the peer as synthetic session input: it schedules the peer, is filed in its inbox as `type: synthetic`, and never renders as a user turn. The text carries an envelope with the sender id, sender title and reply target; the same fields ride in `metadata.ocTalk`. Metadata is not guaranteed to reach the model, so the envelope lives in the text. ## Tools - `talk_send` — deliver one message into a session by id (`ses_...`) or unique title. It admits `POST /api/session/{id}/synthetic`, reports `{id, sessionID, title, from, replyTo, delivered, delivery, deliveryReason}`, and accepts an optional `wait` that returns only messages newer than the send. `delivery: "steer"` is accepted; `delivery: "queue"` is a typed `bad_request`. A leading `[steer]` or `STEER:` is stripped. - `talk_inbox` — read any session's messages as `{id, role, text, tools, time}`, newest first, default 20, including synthetic peer mail. `session` defaults to the calling session; `since` keeps only newer messages, `type` filters, `cursor` pages, and `wait` blocks until the session idles again. Unknown or ambiguous titles return candidates, never a guess. The messaging tools work across sessions, subagents and agents: a reply is a real synthetic message back to the sender. The optional board pair is documented below; it is not part of the default surface. ## Replies, ACKs and terminal rows `talk_send` is fire-and-forget unless the caller passes `wait`. A reply is a choice, not an obligation, and these are prose conventions between peers — the plugin adds no runtime trick and sends nothing on your behalf: - A message that needs an answer says what answer it wants. Only then does the sender call `talk_send` with `wait`, and `wait` reports `timedOut:true` if the peer never reaches a turn boundary. - A peer that is finished and needs no reply ends with a line of `ACK` or `no reply needed`. The sender treats that as terminal and does not wait. - A peer that is handing a task on names the new owner and the seam, then stops. Silence after an ACK is expected, not a failure to be polled forever. ## Board coordination (opt-in) The board pair is **not** part of a default install. A host that already keeps its own coordination board enables it with the `boardFile` option (or an explicit `board: true`) in its own config: ```json { "plugins": [ { "package": "oc-talk", "options": { "boardFile": "" } } ] } ``` The board file and the seam/state convention belong to the **host harness**, not to oc-talk. This package neither creates nor requires that file: a stranger who installs it sees only the two messaging tools above. When opted in: - `talk_board` — read the host's board file and return `rows` of `{session, state, ticket, seam, since}`. A missing file returns an empty list and a clear message, never an error. Read-only. - `talk_claim` — claim a `seam` for the calling session with optional `ticket` and `state` (default `active`), writing a row with an ISO-8601 `since`. A seam held by another session is refused with the holder named, a stale row is never silently stolen, and re-claiming your own seam updates its row instead of adding a duplicate. The file stays plain YAML and is readable without the plugin. A session's own closed rows are dropped on its next claim; other sessions' closed rows keep the newest 20 so history cannot grow into the row cap. - `active` means live work, `parked` means deliberately waiting, and `closed` means finished history. `closed` is the terminal row: a new claim on that seam takes it over without asking. ### Board leases and safe takeover Each claimed row carries an internal lease (a heartbeat and an expiry). Re-claiming your own seam is the heartbeat: it refreshes the lease without another tool call. The five public fields never change, so hand-edited YAML and the `{rows}` tool contract stay compatible with older boards. Another session may take a held seam only with an explicit `talk_claim { "seam": "...", "takeover": true, "reason": "..." }` **and** all four of these hold: the liveness check names that holder, the service answered `session_not_found` for it (a `backend_unavailable`, `timeout` or `backend_error` answer is not proof the holder is gone), the lease has expired, and a reason is recorded on the row. A live lessor is never stolen, a row with no lease is never stolen, and a takeover without a reason is refused. `takeover: false` is a harmless no-op boolean. Claims take a sidecar lock for the whole read-modify-write and compare the file before renaming it, so a hand edit landing mid-claim is reported as `board_changed` instead of silently losing a row. Retry the claim after reading the board again. ### Reading a large board `talk_board` defaults to every row, unchanged. Pass `state`, `seam` or `session` to filter, and `limit` plus the returned `cursor.next` to page. The `rows` shape stays `{session, state, ticket, seam, since}`; a filtered read also reports `total` and `cursor`. `broadcastPlan(sessions, text)` is a read-only helper: it deduplicates targets and returns the `talk_send` calls to make. It adds no tool and sends nothing; `talk_send` typing is unchanged. ## Requirements - OpenCode V2. - Node 22 or newer. - The harness's own local service with a readable state file. No network, no telemetry. ## Status **Unverified** — as-is, use at your own risk. ## Links - [Issues](https://github.com/nathwn12/oc-collections/issues) - [Releases](https://github.com/nathwn12/oc-collections/releases) - [Package source](https://github.com/nathwn12/oc-collections/tree/main/packages/oc-talk) - [MIT licence](https://github.com/nathwn12/oc-collections/blob/main/LICENSE)

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

## [0.7.1] - 2026-11-26

### Fixed

- The public surface is two tools again by default: `talk_send` and `talk_inbox`. The `talk_board` and `talk_claim` pair had shipped unconditionally with the board work, so a stranger installing the package was shown four tools and a host-only `.nstack/board.yaml` convention it never configured. Both board tools are now opt-in: they register only when the host passes the `boardFile` option (or `board: true`), with their descriptions, schemas, file resolution and takeover gates unchanged. The README documents the pair as an optional harness convention.


- npm metadata alignment: README wording and keywords refreshed (cosmetic).
### Added

- `talk_board`: read `<repo>/.nstack/board.yaml` as rows of `{session, state, ticket, seam, since}`; a missing file returns an empty list and a clear message instead of an error. Read-only: it never claims a seam or changes the board.
- `talk_claim`: claim a `seam` for the calling session with an optional `ticket` and `state` (default `active`), writing a row with an ISO-8601 `since`. The file is authoritative and is re-read on every call: a seam held by another session is refused with the holder named (active, parked or closed), a stale row is never silently stolen, and re-claiming your own row updates it in place instead of adding a duplicate. The board stays plain YAML, readable and editable without the plugin.
- `src/board.mjs`: the package's only board-file reader and writer, with the same small fixed-shape contract as the transport seam and no YAML dependency.

### Changed

- The board lock carries an owner token. A stale lock can still be stolen by rename, but its former owner can no longer unlink the lock a new claimant just took.
- Closed rows are bounded history: a session's own closed rows are drained at its next claim, and other sessions' closed rows keep the newest 20.
- `talk_board` reports the resolved `file` and board `version`; a missing board names the path it looked at.

## [0.6.2] - 2026-11-20

Delivery moves off the user prompt and onto the host's synthetic route.

### Changed

- `talk_send` admits `POST /api/session/{id}/synthetic` instead of `POST /api/session/{id}/prompt`. The message is synthetic session input: it schedules the peer, is filed in its inbox as `type: synthetic`, and never renders as a TUI user turn. No `resume` flag is sent, so the host schedules execution.
- Every message carries an envelope in `text`: sender id, sender title and the reply target, then a blank line and the caller's text. The same id and reply target ride in `metadata.ocTalk` with `version: "0.6.2"`, and a short `description` names the sender's title. The envelope stays in `text` because metadata is not guaranteed to reach the model's context.
- `talk_send` reports `from: {sessionID, title}` and `replyTo`. A caller the host does not expose keeps the old bare-text payload and reports `from: null` and `replyTo: null`. A text that already opens with `[oc-talk] from ` is not wrapped again.
- `wait` returns only messages newer than the pre-send baseline, oldest first, as `{role, text}`, capped at 20. The sender's own delivery is excluded.

### Compatibility

- A call no longer triggers a user prompt in the target session. Code that relied on a peer seeing a user turn must read the synthetic mail with `talk_inbox`.

## [0.6.1] - 2026-11-17

### Changed

- Run the offline test suite as part of the package check.

### Fixed

- Respect cancellation and deadlines during session lookup, polling, and reply reads; preserve successful delivery when a later wait or read fails.

## [0.5.0] - 2026-11-13

Queue delivery is removed. Every send steers, and the lane is no longer decided
for the caller.

### Removed

- `delivery: "queue"` and `delivery: "auto"`. `steer` is the only lane: a request naming either removed value is a typed `bad_request` — `queue removed; oc-talk is steer-only` — rather than a silent steer, because changing a caller's lane changes the meaning of what they wrote.
- The urgency classifier, with its halt, correction and deferring phrase tables and the length guard that existed only to keep a long brief from being steered. No wording routes a message any more.
- The `[queue]` and `QUEUE:` delivery markers. They are ordinary text now and are delivered as written.

### Changed

- `wait` is a post-send idle poll, not a lane. It runs after the message was admitted, reads the target's next turn boundary, and cannot change what was sent: a steered message with `wait` is still steered, and a bounded wait that gives up still reports `timedOut: true`.
- `deliveryReason` is one of `explicit`, `marker` or `default`.
- The transport's fallback lane is `steer`, so the wire never carries `queue`.

## [0.4.1] - 2026-11-13

The registry's `0.4.0` is the build before the correction; this release carries the correction.

### Fixed

- `0.4.0` shipped the delivery classifier with a trigger set that fired on bare words, so ordinary handoffs — "don't forget the changelog", "use pnpm instead of npm here" — were steered into a peer's running turn. That trigger set is replaced by two tight tiers and a veto list that beats both: a short message that opens with a halt command, or one that carries an unambiguous correction phrase anywhere, steers; deferring, temporal and substitutional phrasing vetoes both tiers and always queues.
- Marker stripping is correct on a Markdown link: `[queue](https://example.com)` is delivered byte for byte, because a marker is routing only when it is followed by whitespace or the end of the text.
- A body that is only a marker is a typed `bad_request` naming the real problem — there is nothing to deliver — instead of admitting an empty message into the peer.
- A positive `wait` always queues, even with an explicit `delivery: "steer"` or a `[steer]` marker, so the wait reads the boundary after the queued message rather than a boundary reached before a steered message was ever processed.

## [0.4.0] - 2026-11-13

The lane is chosen, not fixed: a correction reaches the peer inside its turn, and a handoff still waits for the next one.

### Added

- `talk_send` takes `delivery`: `auto` (default), `steer` or `queue`. `steer` is admitted into the target's current turn at its next step boundary; `queue` waits for the next turn. Any other value is a typed `bad_request`, and nothing is sent.
- Under `auto` the lane is resolved in this order: a positive `wait`, which always queues; an explicit `delivery`; a leading `[steer]`, `[queue]`, `STEER:` or `QUEUE:` marker, stripped from the delivered text; then two tight correction tiers — a message of 400 characters or fewer that opens with a halt command (`stop`, `halt`, `abort`, `cancel that`, `revert`, `undo`, `roll back`, `hold off`, `don't`, `do not`, `never mind`, `leave it`, `discard`, after at most one leading interjection or the peer's name), or that carries an unambiguous correction phrase anywhere (`that's wrong`, `not what i asked`, `wrong branch`, `wrong file`, `revert that`, `undo it`, `emergency`, `asap`, `urgent`, `immediately`, `credentials are exposed`, `stop the deploy`, …); everything else queues.
- Deferring, temporal and substitutional phrasing vetoes both tiers and always queues, because a false steer interrupts a peer mid-task while a false queue only costs latency: `don't forget`, `do not forget`, `wait for`, `when you are done`, `when you finish`, `instead of`, `no longer needed`, `no longer used`, `if you have time`.
- The reply carries `delivery` and `deliveryReason` (`explicit`, `marker`, `wait`, `urgent`, `handoff`) beside `{id, sessionID, title, delivered}`.

### Changed

- `talk_send` no longer hardcodes `queue`: a short "Stop — the migration is wrong, revert it." reaches the peer's current turn instead of waiting a full turn to be read. A long brief still queues, however many stop words it contains.

### Fixed

- The lane classifier steers only on a real correction. A single context-free token (`wrong`, `failed`, `red`, `critical`, `blocker`, `wait`, `instead`) no longer interrupts a peer: "don't forget to update the changelog", "wait for the build to finish", "the failed test is in the auth file", "cancel the pending release note draft" and "tests are red on main" all queue.
- A marker is routing only when `[steer]`, `[queue]`, `STEER:` or `QUEUE:` is followed by whitespace or the end of the text, so a Markdown link such as `[queue](https://example.com)` arrives byte for byte instead of being delivered mangled.
- A message that is only a marker is a typed `bad_request` naming the real problem — there is nothing to deliver — instead of admitting an empty body into the peer.
- A positive `wait` always queues, even with an explicit `delivery: "steer"` or a `[steer]` marker. The wait then always reads the boundary after the queued message, rather than a boundary reached before a steered message was ever processed.
- The tool description states the rule a calling model needs: `delivery` defaults to `auto`, a short correction or stop steers, a handoff queues, `wait` always queues, and `delivery` or an inline marker overrides `auto` but never `wait`.

## [0.3.0] - 2026-11-13

The surface is two tools. Everything else is gone, and the backend is the local
service over HTTP instead of one CLI child per call.

### Added

- `talk_send`: deliver one message into a session by id or unique title, queued behind the target's current turn, returning the admission (`{id, sessionID, title, delivered}`) in milliseconds; an optional `wait` blocks until the target reaches a turn boundary and returns `{timedOut, waitedMs, messages}`.
- `talk_inbox`: read a session's messages as `{id, role, text, tools, time}`, newest first, default 20; `session` defaults to the calling session, `since` keeps only what is newer, `cursor` pages, and `wait` blocks until a turn boundary first.
- `src/transport.mjs`: the only HTTP client in the package — endpoint resolution from the running service's state, loopback rewrite, one keep-alive agent, and the same four error codes the CLI seam returned.

### Changed

- The transport is HTTP to the running service: `POST /api/session/{id}/prompt` with a client-generated `msg_` id (idempotent retry), `GET /api/session/{id}/message` for reads, and `GET /api/session?search=` for title resolution.
- A turn boundary is read from the message stream (`type: "idle"`) instead of the experimental wait route.

### Removed

- The thirteen lifecycle and conversation tools (`session_list`, `session_send`, `session_read`, `session_close`, `session_open`, `session_kick`, `session_park`, `session_kill`, `session_ask`, `session_wait`, `session_reply`, `session_thread`, `session_broadcast`), the `done` title lock and its prefix state machine, and `docs/GUIDE.md`, which documented that surface.

## [0.1.8] - 2026-11-02

### Changed

- Removed the `session_await` tool (send-then-poll queued messages behind long turns); `session_send` and `session_kick` now default to `steer`.

### Removed

- The `timeoutMs` argument, which only `session_await` took.

## [0.1.7] - 2026-11-01

### Fixed

- Keep one tool registration per host location; a single module-level registration let the second location dispose the first location's tools, so the live service exposed zero oc-talk tools.

## [0.1.6] - 2026-11-01

### Fixed

- `@opencode/plugin` is a runtime dependency; as a peer it was absent from the published install, so the import failed and no tools registered.

## [0.1.5] - 2026-11-01

### Fixed

- Ported to the V2 plugin definition (`Plugin.define`); the previous object export was loaded but never executed, so no tools registered.

## [0.1.4] - 2026-11-01

### Fixed

- Registering tools is idempotent across a plugin reload: `setup` disposes the previous tool-transform registration before creating a new one, so a reload leaves exactly one live registration instead of zero tools until a full restart. The cleanup `setup` returns disposes that registration on unload.

## [0.1.3] - 2026-11-01

### Added

- `delivery` argument on `session_send`, `session_kick`, `session_open` and `session_await`: `steer` preempts the peer's running turn, `queue` waits for it to finish.
- Defaults follow the caller's intent — `session_await` defaults to `steer` (the caller is blocked on the answer), `session_send`, `session_kick` and `session_open` default to `queue` (they must not derail the peer); an explicit value always wins.
- Any other value is a typed `bad_request`, never a silent fallback.

### Changed

- Tool descriptions are at most three sentences each: the when-to-use sentence and the refusal rule stay, the rest is gone.

## [0.1.2] - 2026-11-01

### Changed

- Docs only: the package is published on npm, so the README now gives the registry install route first and keeps the two local checkout routes as the development alternative.

## [0.1.1] - 2026-10-31

### Changed

- Plugin id is `oc-talk` (was `session-talk`); tool names are unchanged.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-10-31

### Added

- `session_list`: every live session as id, title, directory and last-update time.
- `session_send`: one text message to a peer session by id or unambiguous title substring, `resume` defaulting to true so the peer's loop runs.
- `session_read`: a peer's newest messages, newest first, default 20, text verbatim.
- Title resolution is exact-substring and case-sensitive; a missing title returns a typed error with near-misses and an ambiguous title returns a typed error with candidates, never a guess.
- The backend is the `opencode api` CLI spawned with argv and a 20 s timeout, so this package never reads, returns or logs the harness's credentials.
